name: Crownweave
title: The Union of Crownweave
intro: One island in the middle sea. The Crown stands at its heart, ringed by the Crownlands and the Everstorm; Skyloom lies west, Northreach north, Stormwake east and Emberweave south. Choose any town for what the Compendium says of it.

lore.text: A walled river-port on the Newleighin, a day’s ride below the Emberward stormgate. Sea-going ships cannot reach it, but river-lighters can, and the Fjerfian Route brings cargo up from the coast to quays that are, by Emberweave standards, almost orderly.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: The anchor-town. Its plazas cluster around the roots of the Skyward Towers, and its buildings are low and broad so as not to foul the lift-wards. Every afternoon the Loom’s shadow crosses it end to end; shopkeepers set their clocks by it.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: A lake-port on the south-western shore where, by long-standing agreement, the Loomwardens hold the air perfectly still. No wind reaches Stillmere’s mere.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: A tiny citadel on the road south of Castfield where the Weave’s minted coin is held before transfer to The Crown. It has more guards than residents, and no tavern.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.epithet: The Larder and the Fallen Field
lore.text: A market-town that preserves, pickles, and salts much of what the Loom eats. Beyond its northern hedges lies the Fallen Field, where those who fell from the Loom—by accident, by misjudgement at the Dropway, or from Stormwatch Edge—are buried. Of late, several of those graves have been found disturbed from within.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: River-mill and timber towns that feed the southern Weave. Burtonrith’s light, close-grained wood goes to skycraft frames; Holtondon’s mills grind grain and turn tools.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: A plaza-town of kilns and glasshouses where the Union’s finest cloudglass is blown: the thin, pale panes of the Luminous Ward, the crystal of the Halo Overlook, and the lenses of every pressure-gauge sold in the Loft Market.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: River-mill and timber towns that feed the southern Weave. Burtonrith’s light, close-grained wood goes to skycraft frames; Holtondon’s mills grind grain and turn tools.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: The largest town in Skyloom, built around a river crossing and a heavy citadel. Burbotford Keep houses the Weave’s ground-tethered watch and the reserve wings of the Aerialring guard, and its storehouses are the Loom’s pantry of last resort. Bootmakers, cheesewrights, potters, and bronze-smiths crowd its lanes.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: A small walled village that strikes the Union’s supply of Lifesap, the elven coin most associated with Skyloom. Its mint-house is tended by elven assayers who treat each die as a family heirloom. Travellers are not welcome after dark.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: Three towns on the southern and eastern roads that between them arm the Weave. Waringley casts bronze for anchor-chain fittings and wind-ballistae, and raises the sheep whose wool lines Skyloom’s flight-cloaks. Castfield, walled, works the leather and steel of feathersteel harness.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: A jeweller’s village whose settings are made to hold crystal steady against vibration; much favoured by fliers.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: Three towns on the southern and eastern roads that between them arm the Weave. Waringley casts bronze for anchor-chain fittings and wind-ballistae, and raises the sheep whose wool lines Skyloom’s flight-cloaks. Castfield, walled, works the leather and steel of feathersteel harness.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: A citadel on the coastal highlands with a broad, level landing-field for skycraft too heavy to reach the Loom. Its watch-tower is the westernmost manned post in the Union; on clear days its keepers claim to see the green line of Thal’Vireth. Few believe them.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: Three towns on the southern and eastern roads that between them arm the Weave. Waringley casts bronze for anchor-chain fittings and wind-ballistae, and raises the sheep whose wool lines Skyloom’s flight-cloaks. Castfield, walled, works the leather and steel of feathersteel harness.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: Trading posts on the Sapphire Road. Chadon is the clearinghouse for ceramics, boots, and harness bound for the Loft Market; Fercelle makes the long-burning candles that light the Sky Lanes.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: Trading posts on the Sapphire Road. Chadon is the clearinghouse for ceramics, boots, and harness bound for the Loft Market; Fercelle makes the long-burning candles that light the Sky Lanes.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: A hill-city on the north-western heights and the largest settlement of winged folk outside the Aerialring. Windperch keeps the Weave’s ground weather-stations, trains young fliers in open air before they ever approach the Dropway, and distils a strong liquor considered medicinal after a hard landing.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: Skyloom’s great western port, and the only harbor in the Union where mast and mooring-ring share a quay. Sea-going ships tie up below, skycraft moor to tall iron masts above, and cargo is swung between them on cranes. Ships from the western sea—including the rare elven vessel out of Thal’Vireth—make first landfall here.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: A small walled fort on the Old Trail, garrisoned to watch a second rift in the hills to the south—the Gimorand Tear. Unlike the Reach Tear, nothing is sent into it. The garrison’s orders are to report anything that comes out. The orders do not say what to do next.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: A village and a hamlet that supply Gimorand and Windperch with liquor, provisions, and lamp-candles. Aillenestre is kept by an old elven family who have tended the Sky Lane beacons over the Northern Arm for three generations.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: A village and a hamlet that supply Gimorand and Windperch with liquor, provisions, and lamp-candles. Aillenestre is kept by an old elven family who have tended the Sky Lane beacons over the Northern Arm for three generations.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.epithet: Where the Sky Is Put Down
lore.text: At the northern tip of the prefecture stands Skyloom’s strangest city. When the Loom Temple turns a storm away from the Union, the weather has to go somewhere; much of it is sent north and set down here. Skyfall Reach endures more hail, lightning, and sudden rain in a season than the rest of the Union does in a decade.
lore.chapter: Of Skyloom, the Loom Above

lore.text: The Iron Crucible is the largest settlement in the Union outside The Crown itself, and it is not, strictly speaking, a city. It is a town that grew up around a fortress, and then grew into it.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: Northreach strikes more coin than any other Weave, and it does not trust any single site with the whole of it.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: A walled caravanserai on the Crucible’s northern approach, where wagons from the coast rest before the final climb. A short ride beyond its walls lies the Orcholis Aperture: a standing rift in the moor, enclosed by three concentric fences and a Crucible garrison.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: A western highland town over the Reach’s only silver lode, and the principal mint of the Hearthmark, the dwarven coin that is Northreach’s pride. A Hearthmark struck at Pydros carries a small hammer-mark on its rim; coin-weighers in every Weave check for it.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.epithet: The Glass Citadel and the Margin
lore.text: The Reach’s second city, sitting on its southern edge where the highland falls toward The Crown.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: A walled eastern town whose kilns fire the ceramic insulators and pressure-sleeves of the Vessels. Nicea’s potters claim that every Vessel joint in the Reach has passed through their hands at least once. Nobody has bothered to disprove it.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: Northreach strikes more coin than any other Weave, and it does not trust any single site with the whole of it.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: A walled fort on the Skyfall Reach Road where it enters Northreach from Skyloom. Thena inspects everything coming east from the Loom, and keeps bees in its outer yard; its wax and honey are the only sweet things the Reach produces.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: Northreach strikes more coin than any other Weave, and it does not trust any single site with the whole of it.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: Highland villages above the Deepdelve entrances. Calylos keeps the great stairs; Artyntica, one of the Mint Line, strikes coin in a hall cut directly into the rock.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: A plaza-port on the Reach’s north-eastern tip and its door to Stormwake, by sea along the Serpentine Ebon Route and by land along the Newbomyard Trail.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: A port-town on the Frost Coast where the Great Frost Route comes in from the north. Ore, cold-cured timber, and occasional Khazrund cargoes are landed here and sent inland along the Maramersban Path.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: Northreach strikes more coin than any other Weave, and it does not trust any single site with the whole of it.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: Northreach strikes more coin than any other Weave, and it does not trust any single site with the whole of it.
lore.chapter: Of Northreach Weave, the Iron Threshold

lore.text: A port on the northern coast where the Serpentine Ebon Route comes in from Northreach. Cleoverbot is older than Caer Veyn and does not let anyone forget it.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.epithet: Seat of the Weave, and capital of record of the Union
lore.text: Caer Veyn sits at the north-eastern corner of the Weave, where the Harbor Shore turns south into the Wakewater.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: The second city of Stormwake stands inland at the western end of the Weave, where the Amethyst Road sets out for The Crown. Marlmond is where foreign cargo is made respectable. Resins, spices, oils, and aromatics landed in Caer Veyn are brought here to be distilled, blended, rebottled in Marlmond glass, and relabelled as Crownweave goods.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A fort over the white-sand pits from which Cleoverbot and Marlmond make their glass. It is fortified because white sand, left unguarded, tends to walk.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: The Assay Line: Buclester, Skipseade, Widetonces, Newbomyard, and Presterling. See Of Foreign Coin, above. Skipseade and Widetonces also cut the timber for the Wake’s shipyards.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: The Assay Line: Buclester, Skipseade, Widetonces, Newbomyard, and Presterling. See Of Foreign Coin, above. Skipseade and Widetonces also cut the timber for the Wake’s shipyards.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: North of Caer Veyn, on the headland that guards the harbor mouth, the town of Dunscaston casts bronze cannon and the heavier harbor artillery.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: The Assay Line: Buclester, Skipseade, Widetonces, Newbomyard, and Presterling. See Of Foreign Coin, above. Skipseade and Widetonces also cut the timber for the Wake’s shipyards.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: The Assay Line: Buclester, Skipseade, Widetonces, Newbomyard, and Presterling. See Of Foreign Coin, above. Skipseade and Widetonces also cut the timber for the Wake’s shipyards.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A walled village south-west of the bay where amber is dug from old sea-beds. Wihulbover amber is cut into jewellery and charms, and occasionally a piece is found with something inside it that nobody can identify. Those pieces go to Watford.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: Two small settlements between Marlmond and Caer Veyn that make the adzes, augers, caulking irons, and rope-hooks of every shipyard in the Union. Craftry holds a town charter out of all proportion to its size; it was granted in gratitude for the tools that rebuilt the harbor after the Western Gale.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: Two small settlements between Marlmond and Caer Veyn that make the adzes, augers, caulking irons, and rope-hooks of every shipyard in the Union. Craftry holds a town charter out of all proportion to its size; it was granted in gratitude for the tools that rebuilt the harbor after the Western Gale.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A town just west of Caer Veyn that casts lighter guns for merchant escorts and ship’s decks. Marlney-cast pieces are stamped with a knot; captains pay extra for them, and pirates pay extra to take them.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: The Assay Line: Buclester, Skipseade, Widetonces, Newbomyard, and Presterling. See Of Foreign Coin, above. Skipseade and Widetonces also cut the timber for the Wake’s shipyards.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A farming town and a trading post on the western shore, supplying the forts with food and the waiting crews with drink.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A hill-city on the southern headland, where the Caer Veynese Lane leaves the Wakewater for the open sea. Hinckburgh’s weather-readers keep a constant watch on the southern and eastern horizons and exchange signals with Skyloom’s Loomwardens—cordially, now, though Hinckburgh has never entirely forgiven the Western Gale either.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A few hundred paces from Stotfordbu stands a second walled fort, smaller and with a temple of its own. Watford is where arcana confiscated at the Tidecall Exchange are taken to be catalogued, sealed, and reclassified. It also has a shanty-camp, though who lives in it, and why they cannot go home, is not a matter of public record.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A farming town and a trading post on the western shore, supplying the forts with food and the waiting crews with drink.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A small walled fort between Stotfordbu and the Hook, housing the customs cutters that patrol the bay.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A walled citadel on the Wakewater’s eastern shore, with its own temple and a crowded shanty-camp outside its gates. Every ship arriving from beyond the Union’s waters is required to anchor off Stotfordbu until its crew has been examined for plague, curse, and resonance sickness. Crews wait in the camp.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A walled town directly across the Wakewater from Caer Veyn, and the largest settlement on the Hook. By long-standing charter, Nenilton is where foreign merchant houses may own warehouses, keep permanent factors, and live under their own customs—within its walls.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A walled citadel-town at the easternmost point of the Union, looking out toward Emberfall and Khazrund. Reatonsey sees every ship on the Stardust Lane long before Caer Veyn does, and sends word ahead by signal-fire and fast rider along the Whirlwind Road.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: The Hook’s smaller towns, trading post, and fort. Alworth and Harton feed the peninsula; Cleoroughes is the Hook’s own market, where the back-room changers do the business the Assay Line will not; Albrigh is a fort whose garrison watches Nenilton at least as closely as it watches the sea.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A citadel-fort at the Hook’s southern tip, built to hold the Wreckers’ Shallows. It does not hold them. It does, however, hang the ones it catches where the others can see.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: North of Caer Veyn, on the headland that guards the harbor mouth, the town of Dunscaston casts bronze cannon and the heavier harbor artillery.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A river-town and a small walled fort on the Westlands’ northern edge, where the road from Northreach comes down to Marlmond.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A river-town and a small walled fort on the Westlands’ northern edge, where the road from Northreach comes down to Marlmond.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.epithet: City of a Hundred Crowns, Loom of the Realms
lore.text: The city itself: The Crown and its walled Weaves, on a broad hill above the Quatford, where every road in the Union knots together above the Meridian Spire.
lore.chapter: Crownweave

lore.text: A plaza-town on the Witford river where the Amethyst Road, coming south from Marlmond, turns west for The Crown. Witford lives on the turn: coaching inns, remount stables, and the last customs post before the stormgate, where cargo already cleared at the Tidecall is cleared again, more politely, for the Crown’s benefit.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A Crown Guard post on the Loom Road west to Skyloom’s Central District.
lore.chapter: Crownweave

lore.text: A Crown Guard post on the Iron Road north-west to Phais and Northreach, skirting the foot of the Everstorm’s mountain.
lore.chapter: Crownweave

lore.text: A Crown Guard post on the Amethyst Road east to Witford, Marlmond, and Stormwake.
lore.chapter: Crownweave

lore.text: A Crown Guard post on the Ember Road south to Fjerfi and Emberweave.
lore.chapter: Crownweave

lore.text: A walled port at the mouth of the Kingham, and the Union’s nearest harbor to the Iron Hordes. Ships that dare the crossing load and unload here; so do the envoys, mercenaries, and soulstone-traders who make the crossing worth daring.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A plaza-port at the mouth of the Knavereley, the Weave’s door to the eastern sea and to Emberfall’s trade. Spice, dye, resin, and saffron come ashore here, and most of the spice stalls in the city quarter are stocked from its warehouses. Its temple is the only one on the coast with a Dustveil altar and a sea-shrine, and keeps both busy.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A plaza-town at the ford where Skyloom’s southern trails come down to Emberweave, and the first place in the Weave where the grass goes yellow. Cinderford is where caravans bound for the Tableland take on their last cheap water and their first expensive guides.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A river-town north of Emberpeak where the Downs Road comes in from Stormwake. Its kilns, smithies, and wheelwright yards are the dwarven waystations of the city quarter writ large: half the axles and wheel-bands in the south were made or mended here.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A walled river-town on the Saffron Road, built around an Iron-Tusk lodge large enough to be called a fortress. Caravans heading east hire their guards here; caravans arriving from the east report to it, whether or not they meant to.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: Fishing villages along the Burning Coast; Shellhythe’s divers bring up the pearl-shell that Saffron Quay sells as Emberfall work. Charwick and Smokesands cure their catch in smokehouses that stain the whole shore grey; Reedmouth, on the next river east of Brandmouth, takes the overflow when Brandmouth’s harbor is full.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: Fishing villages along the Burning Coast; Shellhythe’s divers bring up the pearl-shell that Saffron Quay sells as Emberfall work. Charwick and Smokesands cure their catch in smokehouses that stain the whole shore grey; Reedmouth, on the next river east of Brandmouth, takes the overflow when Brandmouth’s harbor is full.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A village of pepper-gardens on the river below Fjerfi, and a thorn-hedged hamlet on the Skyloom side whose stock-pens hold the Weave’s spare draught animals.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A coastal village beside the white pans where the Tableland meets the sea. Its salt dries in crusts so clear they are sold as “glass salt” to the Crown’s better kitchens and the Collegium’s worse experiments. The Glass Salt Uprisings began in its salt-yards; see likewise Volume XII.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A walled caravanserai in the dry heart of the Tableland, held by the orc clans whose banners hang in the Iron-Tusk lodges of the city quarter. Every caravan that crosses the west stops at Ashline, pays the clans for passage, and is better guarded for it.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: The Tableland’s upland village, its one dependable well, and its southern fishing cove. Drywell’s water-keepers hold their office by inheritance and keep a ledger of every barrel drawn; there are older entries in it than in Fjerfi’s town charter.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A hamlet of charcoal-burners in the wet woods below Emberpeak, and a fishing village north of Saffron Quay whose red cliffs are mined for vermilion pigment.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A plaza-port at the mouth of the Helscom on the Wakewater’s western shore. Ships too large or too suspect for Caer Veyn’s inner quays lie off Wakefold instead, and its lighters carry their cargo up the shore to the forts and inland to Marlmond.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A plaza-town in the lee of the Downs whose distilleries render the first oils from the fields before the casks go north to Marlmond. In flowering season the whole town smells so strongly of lavender that Marlmond’s perfumers send their apprentices here to ruin their noses on purpose, so they will learn to work by measure instead.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A river village at the point where Stormwake, Emberweave, and the Crownlands meet. Its boundary stone is carved with three crossing threads, and its people are taxed, by long custom, by whichever Warden asks first.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A salt-boiling village on the shore below Gullridge, a farming village on the Stotham river, and a hamlet of reed-cutters behind Wakefold.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: Flower-villages, a river village, and a shepherds’ hamlet on the high Downs. Shepherd’s Down’s sheep are the only thing on the hills not grown for scent, and the shepherds will tell you that the wool smells of lavender anyway.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: Flower-villages, a river village, and a shepherds’ hamlet on the high Downs. Shepherd’s Down’s sheep are the only thing on the hills not grown for scent, and the shepherds will tell you that the wool smells of lavender anyway.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A walled fort on Emberpeak’s summit. From its tower a watch-fire can be seen from Brandmouth to the Emberward stormgate, and on clear nights from the decks of ships halfway to the Iron Hordes. Brandwatch is held by Crown Guard veterans who were sent there, in their words, “to cool off.”
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A mining village on the mountain’s northern shoulder, where the Saffron Road crosses it. Its dwarven-run diggings bring up iron, copper, and a dark heavy ore that Northreach buys without saying why. The slag-heaps that name the village glow faintly after rain.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: The Tableland’s upland village, its one dependable well, and its southern fishing cove. Drywell’s water-keepers hold their office by inheritance and keep a ledger of every barrel drawn; there are older entries in it than in Fjerfi’s town charter.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A village on the bare red ridge south of Fjerfi, named for the long scar of rock the Brand Road climbs. Its people sell water and shade to travellers on the ridge, at prices that make the climb feel longer.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A small walled citadel on the Stotham ridge, high enough to see over the whole inner bay. Its signal-mast relays Hinckburgh’s weather warnings north to Caer Veyn, and the forts’ quarantine flags south to Hinckburgh.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A salt-boiling village on the shore below Gullridge, a farming village on the Stotham river, and a hamlet of reed-cutters behind Wakefold.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A market village where the Downs Road crosses the hill-tracks, and where the flower-farmers sell their harvest to Marlmond’s buyers under the eye of a Merchant’s Guild weigh-master.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: A salt-boiling village on the shore below Gullridge, a farming village on the Stotham river, and a hamlet of reed-cutters behind Wakefold.
lore.chapter: Of Stormwake, the Open Harbor of the East

lore.text: Flower-villages, a river village, and a shepherds’ hamlet on the high Downs. Shepherd’s Down’s sheep are the only thing on the hills not grown for scent, and the shepherds will tell you that the wool smells of lavender anyway.

lore.text: A plaza-town and port at the mouth of the Newleighin, where the Fjerfian Route leaves the sea for the river. Sea-going ships unload into the flat-bottomed lighters that give the town its name, and the lightermen’s guild, which owns every one of them, sets the price of everything that reaches Fjerfi by water.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A plaza-town on the Perstoketon, in the warm valley under Emberpeak’s southern face. Slagbarrow’s ore comes down to it for smelting, Brandmouth’s imports come up to it for sale, and its weekly market is the busiest in the south outside Fjerfi.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A walled caravanserai just below the Emberward stormgate, built around a deep well and a long stone trough. Caravans bound for The Crown water their animals here, wash off the road, and put on whatever they intend to be seen arriving in.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: Two river villages on the Knavereley: Dyewater, whose vats turn the river below it red, blue, or saffron depending on the day, and Oxbow, a ferry-and-cattle village on the great bend upstream.

lore.text: A river village where the Brand Road turns along the coast, a fishing village on the black-sand beach west of Brandmouth, and a cove-village at the prefecture’s south-western tip.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: A fishing village in the palms south of Saffron Quay, and a hamlet of vine-growers in the wet woods inland.
lore.chapter: Of Emberweave, the Burning Gate of the South

lore.text: Fishing villages along the Burning Coast; Shellhythe’s divers bring up the pearl-shell that Saffron Quay sells as Emberfall work. Charwick and Smokesands cure their catch in smokehouses that stain the whole shore grey; Reedmouth, on the next river east of Brandmouth, takes the overflow when Brandmouth’s harbor is full.

lore.text: Two fords on the Tableland’s rivers: Dustford, where the coast trail from Skyloom crosses the Mitfordling, and Tawnyford, a herders’ hamlet in the tawny grass below Highdust.

lore.text: A village at the western foot of the mountain, where the Perstoketon comes off its slopes. Brandfoot’s goats are the only creatures that climb Emberpeak for pleasure.
